title: Take a Short App Break Without Ending Your Blocking Routine
description: For a short break from blocked apps, choose an available temporary unlock and check the blocking state again when the break ends.
direct: Use a temporary unlock when you need brief access during a block. Choose the shortest practical break and check that the block resumes.
figureAlt: A face-down phone, one-task note and five-minute break timer.
figureCaption: AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an App screenshot, measured result or real export.
cards.choice.heading: Give the break one purpose
cards.choice.body: Write down the message or task you intend to handle. Choose the shortest available period that fits it. A timer does not stop a feed from being tempting, so leave the app when the task is finished rather than trying to use every remaining minute.
sections.explain.heading: Check the actual boundary
sections.explain.body: A temporary unlock is deliberate access, not a guarantee against bypassing settings. Blocking depends on the selected apps, current permissions and active session or schedule. Test the boundary before relying on it during an important work period.
sections.practice.heading: Keep routines simple
sections.practice.body: One scheduled rule and unlimited thirty-minute Block Now sessions are free; Pro adds unlimited scheduled rules. Temporary unlocks are listed as five, fifteen or thirty minutes. Notifications are optional and are not a substitute for checking the blocking state. The life grid is a reflection tool, not a medical prediction. This workflow makes no promise about productivity or a guaranteed reduction in screen time.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Which break length makes sense for one message?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: Start with the shortest available five-minute option if it covers the task. Choose a longer break only if you know you need it.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: How do I check that blocking resumed?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Open a selected app after the break should end. If it is still available, check the active rule, the app selection and Screen Time permission.

steps.step-1.text: In Dying Soon: Screen Time Limit, keep your selected app-blocking routine active and use its temporary-unlock option when needed.
steps.step-2.text: Choose an available five-, fifteen- or thirty-minute pause. Complete the intended task and close the distracting app.
steps.step-3.text: After the selected interval, try a selected app and confirm the expected blocking state. Review Screen Time authorization and your active routine if it is not as expected.
